Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Confirms Major Expansion to Boost Output in Jordan

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co has announced a significant expansion project aimed at increasing its refining capacity and supporting energy security in Jordan. The initiative, valued at approximately $600 million, will see the company upgrade its existing facilities in Zarqa, northeast of Amman, over the next three years.

The planned expansion is designed to raise the refinery’s crude processing capacity by 30%, from 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 156,000 bpd. The project will focus on modernizing core processing units, enhancing product quality, and introducing advanced environmental controls in line with international standards.

“The expansion is a strategic step to meet the growing domestic demand for refined products and to reduce reliance on imports,” said Eng. Ahmed Al-Saadi, CEO of Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, at a press briefing. “We are committed to ensuring Jordan’s energy needs are met efficiently and sustainably.”

The company stated that local engineering and construction firms, including Al-Tariq Engineering and Petra Industrial Services, will participate in the project, expected to generate over 1,000 temporary jobs during the construction phase.

Industry analysts have welcomed the move, noting the positive impact on Jordan’s balance of trade and local supply chains. “This investment reflects confidence in the sector’s long-term prospects and will improve Jordan’s self-sufficiency in refined petroleum products,” said Rami Khalil, an energy sector consultant based in Amman.

The Jordanian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources expressed support for the expansion, highlighting its alignment with national energy strategies. The ministry emphasized that the project will help ensure a stable supply of gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel for local consumers and industries.

Construction is set to begin in the third quarter of 2024, with full operational capacity targeted for late 2027.
